title: Approval Gate Presets & Audit Triage — Private Deployments (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This draft defines a small set of reusable approval-gate presets and an accompanying audit-triage playbook for Private deployments where customers manage parts of networking (VPC, peering, customer-managed NATs). The goal is to make operator decisions consistent, auditable, and automatable while preserving the low-friction handoff model we promise to enterprise customers.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Approval gate presets (policy templates) for common customer-network changes tied to Private installations: VPC attach/detach, route propagation changes, BGP/peering updates, IP allowlist rules, and control-plane agent upgrades.
- Audit log schema recommendations and correlation keys to join control-plane logs with on-prem/private agent logs.
- Triage playbook for security/ops when gated changes generate anomalies or failed approvals.
- Rollout notes for adding presets to the console and policy-as-code registry.

Out of scope: per-customer bespoke networking designs, deep networking RFCs, and on-prem install instructions (those live in the handover guide).

High-level goals:
1) Provide 6 canonical gate presets that cover ~80% of changes customers request during onboarding and support cycles.
2) Ensure every gated decision emits consistent, queryable audit events with correlation identifiers shared between the control plane and private agents.
3) Create a triage runbook that reduces mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) and mean-time-to-resolve (MTTR) for approval-related incidents.

Personas:
- Platform Engineer (customer): requests changes and expects transparent audit trails.
- Redwood Site Reliability/Support: validates gated changes, performs triage, and escalates.
- Product Ops / Sales Engineer: approves exceptions and provides customer guidance.

Approval gate presets (initial set):
1. VPC-Pairing-Request: For customers who request Redwood agents to attach/detach to/from a customer VPC. Checks: CIDR overlap, required routes, and KMS policy availability. Risk level: medium. Default timeout: 48h.\n2. Route-Propagation-Change: Changes to route tables that affect agent reachability (add/remove routes, propagate new subnets). Checks: critical subnet flag, last-known-agent-count. Risk: high for core subnets. Default timeout: 24h.\n3. External-Peering-Update: BGP session changes or peering neighbor IP updates. Checks: ASN mismatch, origin-as sanity, prefix-lists. Risk: high. Requires two approvers by default.\n4. Control-Plane-Agent-Upgrade: Rolling upgrade of private agents (minor/patch/major). Checks: agent health, pending logs backlog, recent control-plane errors. Risk: low/medium depending on version delta. Default rollback window: 1hr after rollout.\n5. IP-Allowlist-Change: Customer-managed firewall or ingress allowlist updates (control plane endpoints). Checks: overlapping wildcard entries, presence of emergency-access CIDRs. Risk: medium.\n6. Telemetry-Redaction-Policy: Changes to what agent telemetry (logs/metrics) is sent to Redwood. Checks: PII flag, retention overrides, KMS encryption configuration. Risk: compliance-sensitive; require compliance approver.

Each preset includes: human-readable description, structured policy-as-code (YAML/JSON template), default approvers, required artifacts, and minimum audit fields to emit.

Policy-as-code model notes:
- Policies stored in a Git-backed registry per-customer (separate branch per account). Changes to presets create PRs and require at least one product-owner approval.
- Policies are evaluated by the control plane policy engine before enqueuing actions to private agents; failures return structured error codes with guidance.

Audit log schema (recommended canonical fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (UUID, generated at request creation)
- request_id (incoming API call id)
- customer_id (tenant id)
- preset_id (one of the six canonical ids)
- action (create/approve/reject/execute/fail/rollback)
- actor (redwood:user|redwood:system|customer:email or service-account)
- approver_list (comma-separated approver ids)
- approver_decision_reasons (short text)
- control_plane_node (id)
- agent_node_ids (comma-separated list when applicable)
- correlation_keys (comma-separated key=value pairs; see below)
- delta_summary (short human-readable summary of config change)
- retention_class (standard/extended/legal-hold)

Correlation keys: to tie logs across systems we recommend emitting three persistent keys on every record: customer_id, event_id, and request_trace (W3C traceparent or equivalent). Private agent logs should copy event_id and request_trace when executing or responding to a gated action.

Retention and access controls:
- Default retention: 180 days for standard events.
- Extended retention (customer-configurable): 2y or legal-hold.
- Access: RBAC enforced; audit log reads require read-audit role. Logs flagged as PII must be redacted in the default UI and only available via secure export with data access approvals.
- KMS/HSM: all persisted audit blobs must support envelope encryption with customer KMS keys in Private deployments.

Triage playbook (step-by-step):
1) Incident detected: alert fires (failed approval, mismatched CIDR, agent rejection).
2) Support engineer queries audit-event(event_id) in the console and fetches agent logs using correlation keys.
3) Quick checks (safe to run as read-only): recent agent health, route table snapshot, last successful attach.
4) If approvals show conflicting decisions (e.g., multiple approvers with different timestamps), escalate to product-ops and freeze automated execution.
5) For agent-side failures (e.g., replay backlog), perform controlled retry via a policy that records retry_count and backoff.
6) If a security-sensitive change was approved incorrectly (PII or exfil risk flagged), trigger legal-hold retention and start compliance incident process.

Metrics and SLOs for the feature:
- Gate decision latency: median decision time < 6h, 95th < 48h (for default approver set).
- Audit availability: 99.9% of events queryable within 1 minute of emission.
- Correlation fidelity: >= 99% of execution logs must include event_id linking back to a gating record.

UI and operator ergonomics notes:
- Console UI should show a condensed timeline: request -> approval(s) -> execution -> success/failure with links to agent logs (pre-filtered by trace/request id).
- Support view adds ‘diff’ view of requested change, an inline risk badge, and a one-click export for compliance.

Security & compliance considerations:
- Approver identity must be strongly authenticated (SSO + 2FA).
- Emergency bypass paths must be auditable and limited to named role holders; bypass events are flagged and require post-hoc review.
- Exported audit bundles should be signed and checksum-verified.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal pilot): use 5 internal customers / sandbox accounts. Validate correlation keys, retention settings, and triage flows.
- Phase 1 (early customers): enable presets for customers with existing Private deployments; collect feedback and refine default approvers.
- Phase 2 (general availability): add presets to console templates and publish policy-as-code docs.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should default approver sets be global or per-tenant? (proposed: per-tenant with a global sane default)
- Default retention class for high-volume customers—should we provide smart tiering based on the event type?
- Approver quorum: require two approvers for high-risk presets by default? (proposed: external-peering and route-propagation)

Next steps / action items:
- Diego: draft YAML templates for the six presets (due 2024-09-26).
- Priya: prototype audit event schema in staging and verify correlation fidelity (due 2024-10-10).
- Liam: mock up console timeline UI and export workflow (due 2024-10-03).
- Product review session: schedule with SRE and Legal (target week of 2024-10-14).

Notes to reviewers: this is intended as a pragmatic working draft. I'm intentionally keeping preset semantics compact so we can ship something that covers the majority of cases and iterate. Feedback requested on retention defaults, quorum settings, and whether the telemetry-redaction preset is better modeled as a separate compliance workflow.

Raw sketch artifacts / references:
- A minimal policy template example: YAML scaffold to be included in the linked PR (see linked_artifacts).
- Example audit query for support: select * from audit_events where event_id = "<uuid>"; then fetch agent logs with trace=<traceparent>.

-- end of draft --
